messages:
amy_billing: Heads-up — CloudShift (enterprise) flagged their Feb invoice: +12% vs reserved commit. They claim traffic failed over to ap-southeast and got billed burst. attaching their snippet.

maria_finance: please paste invoice id and any meter lines you have. need to know which bucket the meters used.

amy_billing: INV-CS-2026-02 ; vendor excerpt: 'during a 2h failover window on 2026-02-14, traffic routed to ap-southeast and resulted in unexpectedly high burst charges.'

sam_ops: quick sanity: their reserved pool is eu-central only. we don't auto-propagate reserved capacity cross-region unless customer sets multi-region failover -> reserved. fallback behavior is to use shared burst.

lee_product: do we show any recent policy changes? i thought we had a toggle to mark some tenants as "cross-region reserved" for DR. maybe CloudShift didn't enable it.

sam_ops: checked policy history: no toggle flips. however there was a short routing anomaly at 02:12 UTC that sent ~620k tokens through ap-southeast. metering lines below (sanitized):
```
meter: customer=cloudshift region=ap-southeast bucket=burst tokens=420000 ts=2026-02-14T02:22:11Z
meter: customer=cloudshift region=ap-southeast bucket=burst tokens=200000 ts=2026-02-14T03:05:03Z
meter: customer=cloudshift region=eu-central bucket=reserved tokens=1_250_000 ts=2026-02-14T01:10:00Z
```

sam_ops: total burst tokens in APAC ~620k. looks consistent with their complaint.

maria_finance: what's our unit burst rate for that plan? also is there any SLA clause about cross-region failover accounting?

amy_billing: plan uses graduated rates. for enterprise it's flat $0.0045/token for burst.

lee_product: contract note: CloudShift's enterprise addendum states "reasonable DR failover behavior" but doesn't explicitly promise cross-region reserved mirroring. it's a gray area — sales may have implied more.

rico_sales: they were verbally told failover would preserve reserved capacity where possible. we need to avoid damaging the relationship. recommend offering a one-time billing remediation and clarifying the contract.

maria_finance: options: full refund of APAC burst tokens during window (~620k * $0.0045 = $2,790), partial credit, or treat as formal SLA credit if ops finds platform error. we should limit goodwill to under $3k unless CFO okays more.

sam_ops: i'll open OPS-6198 to review whether routing should have picked tenant reserved nodes in eu-central for failover requests. ETA 48h. if it's a platform bug, we should do formal SLA credit. if it's config/contract mismatch, goodwill credit.

amy_billing: draft customer reply: "Thanks — we see the spike. We're issuing a provisional credit and investigating. Will update within 48h with details and final resolution." ok?

rico_sales: good. keep it conciliatory and include an invite to a short technical call.

maria_finance: @david_cfo authorize provisional credit up to $3k while ops investigates? we can reconcile later.

david_cfo: approve provisional credit up to $3k. require memo with final token math, unit rates, and OPS RCA before closing.

billing-bot: export generated: s3://redwood-metering/exports/cloudshift/2026-02-14/1809999999-export.csv

amy_billing: doing calc: 620000 tokens * $0.0045 = $2,790 provisional credit. i'll create credit memo and mark invoice INV-CS-2026-02 as "under review" in billing UI.

maria_finance: once memo is ready route to me for posting and to legal if we need contract addendum.

lee_product: also logging a product action item: add a "failover-billing-tag" for short-term so ops can mark windows as under review to prevent auto-ingestion into invoices. ticket PROD-5142.

amy_billing: sent hold note to CloudShift and issued the provisional credit. included line: "subject to final RCA; provisional credit $2,790 applied."

david_cfo: good. leave thread open until OPS-6198 completes.

amy_billing: closing for now but will update when OPS RCA lands. :white_check_mark:
